documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs; DoIT; Student Success and Enrollment Management
documents.title: HU Policy on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The policy says students "may use AI tools in accordance with course-specific guidance" and that "Faculty determine and communicate course-level AI policies in syllabi and assignments"; it sets no single rule itself and hands the decision to instructors, with only an unauthorized-use ban and data rules as limits.
documents.summary: Hampton's April 2026 university-wide policy sets principles for responsible AI use by students, faculty and administrators. It leaves student use to instructors' course-level rules, bars unauthorized AI completion of graded work, and sets data-privacy, human-review and detector limits. It also covers administrative uses of agentic AI.

units.why: The Purpose states the policy "establishes principles and standards for the responsible, ethical, and lawful use" of AI, which is an institution-level framework preamble (P56), not a rule on a specific use.
units.anchor: establishes principles and standards for the responsible, ethical, and lawful
units.frag_end: upholding the University’s values of integrity, accountability, and fairness

units.why: The sentence says the policy "supports academic excellence, innovation, and institutional operations" while ensuring compliance, privacy and security; it is purpose and rationale, so P56 framework rather than P44 (no professional-skill claim).
units.anchor: supports academic excellence, innovation, and institutional operations

units.why: "applies to all faculty, staff, students, contractors, and affiliates" sets who and what the policy covers, i.e. scope, which P61 defines as definitions setting what a policy covers.
units.anchor: applies to all faculty, staff, students, contractors, and affiliates who use AI
units.frag_end: on behalf of Hampton University or using University resources.

units.why: "Responsible offices include the Office of Academic Affairs" names who owns the policy; fits P56 framework (scope and ownership) since no maintenance cycle is stated here.
units.anchor: Responsible offices include the Office of Academic Affairs;

units.why: The definition "Machine-based systems that, for a given set of" is a definition of AI that sets what the policy covers (P61).
units.anchor: Artificial Intelligence (AI): Machine-based systems that

units.why: The definition of agentic AI as "Autonomous systems powered by large language models" sets the scope of agentic tools covered, so P61.
units.anchor: Autonomous systems powered by large language models (LLMs)

units.why: The definition of GAI as systems that "generate new content, including but not limited to text, images, audio, video, and computer code" defines generative AI, so P61.
units.anchor: generate new content, including but not limited to text, images, audio, video, and computer code

units.why: The definition of "Restricted Data" as "confidential or sensitive, including FERPA-protected records" defines the data category that later privacy rules protect; it is a definition so P61.
units.anchor: Information classified by Hampton University as confidential or sensitive

units.why: The Fair Use definition ("limited use of copyrighted material without permission") is a copyright definition; P52 covers copyright and licensing, and a pure definition could be P61, but it concerns copyright so P52.
units.anchor: limited use of copyrighted material without permission
units.frag_start: Fair Use: A legal doctrine permitting
units.frag_end: Section 107 of the U.S. Copyright Act.

units.why: "AI may be used at Hampton University to enhance learning, teaching, research" is a default statement that AI is allowed for these purposes, so P02 permit by default.
units.anchor: AI may be used at Hampton University to enhance learning, teaching, research

units.why: "users are accountable for outputs they generate or rely upon" makes users responsible for AI output, matching P29 ownership of what is submitted or used.
units.anchor: users are accountable for outputs they generate or rely upon

units.why: "Transparent – use of AI is disclosed where appropriate" requires disclosure of AI use where appropriate, so P24.
units.anchor: use of AI is disclosed where appropriate

units.why: "Ethical – aligned with academic integrity and institutional values" is a principle tying AI use to integrity; no specific rule, so framework P56.
units.anchor: aligned with academic integrity and institutional values

units.why: "Secure – protects sensitive and restricted data" is a principle requiring data protection, matching P50.
units.anchor: protects sensitive and restricted data

units.why: "decisions remain subject to human judgment and oversight" says humans keep final judgment over AI-informed decisions; closest is P32 (humans remain decision-makers) rather than P46, which is only about grades.
units.anchor: decisions remain subject to human judgment and oversight

units.why: "Students may use AI tools in accordance with course-specific guidance" lets course guidance set the rule, so P04 (per-instructor or course decision) with a permissive default conditioned on the course.
units.anchor: Students may use AI tools in accordance with course-specific guidance

units.why: "AI may be used for brainstorming, outlining, language support, tutoring, and skills development when permitted by the instructor" lists several allowed uses; I choose P15 (brainstorming) as the first-named use, though tutoring (P12) and language support (P18) are also listed; the sentence is one policy.
units.anchor: AI may be used for brainstorming, outlining, language support, tutoring, and skills development

units.why: "Use of AI to complete assignments, exams, or graded work without authorization is prohibited" bans AI producing submitted work unless authorized, so P19 (not P22, since it covers all graded work).
units.anchor: Use of AI to complete assignments, exams, or graded work without authorization is prohibited

units.why: "Students must acknowledge and cite AI use when required" requires acknowledging and citing AI use, so P24; the "when required" condition keeps it from being universal.
units.anchor: Students must acknowledge and cite AI use when required

units.why: "responsible for verifying the accuracy and integrity of AI-generated content" requires verification of output, so P31.
units.anchor: responsible for verifying the accuracy and integrity of AI-generated content

units.why: "Restricted Data must not be entered into AI tools" for students prohibits entering confidential data into AI, which is data protection P50 (P20 is about assignment specs and code).
units.anchor: Restricted Data must not be entered into AI tools

units.why: "Violations will be addressed under the Hampton University Student Code of Conduct" routes student AI violations into the conduct process, so P36.
units.anchor: Violations will be addressed under the Hampton University Student Code of Conduct

units.why: "Faculty use of AI should uphold academic freedom while ensuring instructional integrity and fairness" guides how faculty use AI in teaching; P59 covers instructor use in general terms.
units.anchor: uphold academic freedom while ensuring instructional integrity and fairness

units.why: "Faculty determine and communicate course-level AI policies in syllabi and assignments" both delegates (P04) and requires communication in syllabi (P09); I choose P09 because the actionable obligation is to communicate, and P04 is the delegation already coded from the student section.
units.anchor: Faculty determine and communicate course-level AI policies in syllabi and assignments

units.why: "AI detection tools must not be used as the sole basis for academic misconduct determinations" limits reliance on detectors, so P39.
units.anchor: AI detection tools must not be used as the sole basis

units.why: "AI may support teaching, assessment design, feedback, and research, with appropriate review for accuracy and bias" says what faculty may use AI for in teaching work, so P59.
units.anchor: AI may support teaching, assessment design, feedback, and research

units.why: "Restricted Data, unpublished student work, and confidential research materials must not be entered into AI systems without DoIT approval" protects data and student work; P50 fits (privacy) rather than P49, which concerns course materials uploaded by students.
units.anchor: unpublished student work, and confidential research materials must not be entered into AI systems

units.why: "Faculty are expected to model ethical, transparent, and responsible AI use" sets an expectation for faculty conduct; closest is P47 (instructor transparency about own AI use).
units.anchor: Faculty are expected to model ethical, transparent, and responsible AI use

units.why: "AAI may be used to increase student service operations that support advising, retention, and graduation" permits agentic AI for student services; it is administrative use, not teaching, and no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: AAI may be used to increase student service operations that support advising, retention, and graduation.
units.frag_start: AAI may be used to increase
units.uncovered_note: Permits agentic AI for administrative student-service operations (advising, retention, graduation); not teaching or learning use.

units.why: "These agents may be used to enhance operational workflows, communications, data analysis, and service delivery, provided outputs are reviewed" permits administrative AI use with review; no type for administrative operations, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: provided outputs are reviewed for accuracy and appropriateness
units.uncovered_note: Permits agentic AI for operational workflows, communications and data analysis with output review; administrative use.

units.why: "must be reviewed by a human prior to use" requires human review of AI outputs in official operations; P32 and P46 do not fit (not students or grades), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: must be reviewed by a human prior to use
units.frag_end: decision-support must be reviewed by a human prior to use
units.uncovered_note: Human review required before AI outputs are used in official university operations, communications or decision support.

units.why: "AI may not be used to make final decisions regarding employment, finances, academic standing, or disciplinary actions" extends beyond grades, which P46 covers, so UNCOVERED human oversight of institutional decisions.
units.anchor: AI may not be used to make final decisions regarding employment, finances, academic standing, or
units.frag_start: AI may not be used to make
units.uncovered_note: No AI final decisions on employment, finances, academic standing or discipline without human oversight; broader than grading (P46).

units.why: "Restricted Data must not be entered into AI systems without DoIT approval" for administrative use is a data-protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: Restricted Data must not be entered into AI systems without DoIT approval

units.why: "AI must not be used for discriminatory practices, unauthorized surveillance" names harms to avoid, so P53.
units.anchor: AI must not be used for discriminatory practices, unauthorized surveillance

units.why: "All AI use must comply with Hampton University’s data governance, information security, and acceptable use policies" is a data-security rule, P50.
units.anchor: must comply with Hampton University’s data governance, information security, and acceptable use policies
units.frag_start: All AI use must comply with

units.why: "Users must consult DoIT prior to using AI tools that process sensitive or restricted data" is a privacy rule requiring consultation, P50.
units.anchor: Users must consult DoIT prior to using AI tools that process sensitive or restricted data

units.why: "AI tools may not be used to facilitate academic dishonesty" bans AI-enabled dishonesty for everyone; the closest type is P36 (misuse as misconduct).
units.anchor: AI tools may not be used to facilitate academic dishonesty

units.why: The same sentence bans AI to "violate intellectual property rights", an IP rule, so P52 (separate from the dishonesty rule).
units.anchor: violate intellectual property rights

units.why: The sentence also bans AI to "generate or distribute misinformation" and for "harassment, discrimination", harms covered by P53.
units.anchor: generate or distribute misinformation

units.why: "Violations will be addressed through applicable student, faculty, or staff disciplinary processes" says misuse goes to disciplinary processes, P36.
units.anchor: Violations will be addressed through applicable student, faculty, or staff disciplinary processes

units.why: "The Division of Information Technology may restrict access to AI tools that pose institutional risk" lets DoIT block tools; no type covers institutional tool restriction (P50 only prefers vetted tools), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: may restrict access to AI tools that pose institutional risk
units.uncovered_note: IT division may restrict access to AI tools posing institutional risk.

units.why: "will provide ongoing education and professional development to promote responsible AI use" commits the university to training, matching P63 (addressed to all users, nearest fit).
units.anchor: will provide ongoing education and professional development to promote responsible AI use

units.why: "will be reviewed periodically by the Office of the Provost" sets a review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: will be reviewed periodically by the Office of the Provost

notes: Single included document. Several administrative-use rules (agentic AI for student services, human review of AI outputs, no AI final decisions, IT tool restriction) were coded UNCOVERED because the closed list has no administrative-operations type.
